When fighting gravity, you want to minimize the amount of time you're fighting it, which generally means maximum acceleration/deceleration maneuvers, and being at maximum speeds for as long as possible. When fighting wind resistance, it's kind of the other thing around... if you double your speed you square your wind resistance. So on launch, for instance, you WANT to get to an orbital trajectory as fast as possible thanks to gravity (Accelerating at 1m/s^2 forever will eventually get you to orbit if it weren't for fuel), but you CAN'T go too fast thanks to wind resistance. Striking the right balance of doing it quickly but not TOO quickly is where you get your fuel savings. And it just so happens that terminal velocity (at the given air density of the moment and ballistic coefficient) is the optimum speed for the entire exit from the atmosphere.
